column1: # About This Edition after John's ruling on British spelling and older words, 2026-11-04.

column2: Compound words are written as one where we now write them so (shellfish, pineapple, halfway), and old words are given in ours (there for thither, until then for hitherto, every now and then for ever and anon).
column3: Compound words are written as one where we now write them so (shellfish, pineapple, halfway). Kingston’s British spelling (colour, harbour, centre) and his older words (thither, hitherto) are kept, though every now and then stands for ever and anon.
